hypotheses.claim: Foreign-effect closure on Linux requires authority-carrier semantics in addition to path/network/syscall effect declarations.
hypotheses.mechanism: Pre-opened/inherited file descriptors, connected sockets, SCM_RIGHTS, Linux capabilities, environment credentials and other live handles can carry effective authority independently of later pathname checks.
hypotheses.prediction: A child can perform a protected effect through an inherited or received authority-bearing handle while direct pathname access is denied.
current_evidence: Linux Landlock and unix(7) primary documentation
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Complete pathname/syscall mediation alone can indirectly eliminate all relevant authority carriers without representing them as first-class effect/capability objects.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production-relevant target-host enforcement proof demonstrates that no undeclared carrier can survive or enter a child across the supported foreign-code surfaces while the carrier itself is absent from the semantic contract.

hypotheses.claim: A layered Ubuntu Foreign Effect Closure Gate can enforce EffectiveEffects(child) subseteq ParentGrantedEffects union ExternalGrant(receipt) for the supported foreign-code surfaces without a ClayCode semantic redesign.
hypotheses.mechanism: Before child execution, deterministically derive an enforcement plan from the parent Clay effect contract: scrub undeclared descriptors/environment/credentials, drop Linux authority, set no_new_privs, apply supported Landlock restrictions, install seccomp filters, apply resource cgroup limits, constrain IPC/network namespaces or brokers where required, and admit only explicit host/WASI capabilities.
hypotheses.prediction: On Andreas' Ubuntu developer host, adversarial inherited-FD/SCM_RIGHTS/capability/env/syscall/resource probes will fail closed while the ordinary BASE application suite remains functional under explicitly granted capabilities.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Linux enforcement gaps or the required restrictions impose unacceptable utility/complexity cost, so the subset contract cannot be soundly realized for all current foreign-code surfaces with the proposed stack.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any supported child obtains an undeclared effect, or a required normal BASE application cannot run without ambient authority that cannot be represented and safely scoped.

hypotheses.claim: WASI is a useful low-ambient foreign-code backend but cannot by itself establish Clay's full foreign-effect closure theorem.
hypotheses.mechanism: WASI starts from host-provided capabilities/imports, preopens and network grants, which maps well to Clay capability contracts; however host configuration, runtime imports, terminal/host side effects and outer native process authority remain part of the trusted enforcement surface.
hypotheses.prediction: A tightly configured WASI child will require fewer ambient-carrier scrub rules than Python/Bash/native children, but an overbroad host preopen/import/network grant will still widen effective authority.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: For the WASM-only subset, the runtime sandbox and a minimal WasiCtx are sufficient and no outer Clay-specific effect-closure layer adds meaningful protection.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched WASI tests show the outer effect-closure layer contributes no additional detection, containment or receipt fidelity under all supported host configurations.

hypotheses.claim: Effect-closure translation validation should be expressed as a coverage receipt, not only as a pass/fail sandbox launch.
hypotheses.mechanism: For every required semantic effect/restriction atom, record the concrete Ubuntu enforcement mechanism, kernel/runtime feature version, inherited-handle allowlist, unsupported atoms, external grants, policy hash and resource limits. Fail closed when a required restriction lacks enforcement coverage.
hypotheses.prediction: Coverage receipts will expose silent host-version gaps such as unavailable Landlock rights or unconfined IPC channels before execution rather than allowing a weaker-than-declared sandbox.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The receipt becomes a stale paper model that increases complexity without predicting real enforcement failures better than direct integration tests.
hypotheses.falsifier: Mutation tests change effective authority while leaving the proposed receipt semantically identical, or receipt coverage repeatedly predicts safety where target-host adversarial tests escape.

hypotheses.claim: The current evidence does not justify changing ClayCode G9 semantics; the next move is Runtime/ABI/FFI implementation and executable counterexample testing.
hypotheses.mechanism: The current project already has capability/resource/effect identity concepts and a policy of preserving semantics unless a real program proves the language cannot represent the requirement. The discovered failure is presently an enforcement-realization gap, not yet a representation impossibility.
hypotheses.prediction: An effect-closure prototype can encode handle identity, grant provenance and host enforcement coverage using existing ClayCode structures plus runtime metadata.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: G9 cannot represent first-class authority-bearing handles, nested grant provenance or partial host-enforcement coverage without an explicit semantic extension.
hypotheses.falsifier: A concrete ClayCode program/IR example demonstrates that the necessary carrier/grant/coverage distinction cannot be expressed without ambiguity or semantic escape hatch.

hypotheses.claim: Foreign-effect closure can preserve high ordinary developer utility if grants are task-scoped rather than globally restrictive.
hypotheses.mechanism: Build/test/debug/admin tasks receive explicit narrow writable roots, process/network/resource capabilities and time-bounded handles; destructive protected-state effects remain absent or externally brokered.
hypotheses.prediction: The BASE CLI/HTTP/DB/concurrent/GUI/compiler/GPU/system-effect/FRANK-component suite will retain near-baseline task success with bounded overhead while adversarial undeclared-effect tests are rejected.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Real developer workflows depend so heavily on ambient authority and dynamic discovery that explicit scoping causes unacceptable breakage or prompts broad grants that erase the safety benefit.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched utility tests show substantial task failure/latency burden unless grants are widened enough to restore the same protected-damage surface as baseline.

promotion_boundary: No hypothesis is promoted to canonical scientific truth by this spawn run. H-SPAWN-C1-01 has strong mechanism-level support but still lacks exhaustive carrier enumeration and target-host enforcement proof.
